captions.detailed: A realistic road bicycle triple crankset assembly consisting of a central bottom-bracket shell, two opposing light grey crank arms, and three concentric dark grey chainrings. The main drive side includes spider arms that support the chainrings, while both crank arms terminate in black pedals. The spindle and crank arms are designed to rotate continuously around the bottom-bracket axis, and each pedal rotates continuously about its own spindle axis.
captions.instruction: Generate a parameterized 3D model of a road bicycle triple crankset with a bottom bracket. The assembly must include a bottom-bracket shell, two opposing crank arms (drive and non-drive sides), three concentric chainrings supported by a five-arm spider structure, and rotating black pedals attached to each arm. Define continuous rotational joints for the spindle/crank rotation and for each pedal.
captions.factory: Construct a fixed bottom-bracket shell using a cylinder primitive. Create a rotating spindle/crank assembly as a single continuous-jointed part, combining the spindle cylinder, two opposing elongated crank arms, a 5-spoke spider hub, and three concentric thin cylinders representing the triple chainrings. Finally, build two black pedal bodies using box primitives, attaching each to its respective crank arm tip with a continuous revolute joint to model pedal rotation.
